translation.This provider has no record of that addr: This provider has no record of that address, so it has never appeared on chain. Paste the wallet’s stake address instead - that works even for a brand-new address.

translation.None of these addresses has any transact: None of these addresses has any transactions. Wallets show a fresh receive address by default - check this is an address you have actually used, on the right network. Bitcoin has no account view, so Coineda can only see the addresses you list here.
translation.Synced {{label}}, but it has no events a: Synced {{label}}, but it has no events at all
translation.Add an account xpub, or one or more addr: Add an account xpub, or one or more addresses under advanced options.
translation.That is a PRIVATE key. Coineda only ever: That is a PRIVATE key. Coineda only ever needs the public one - paste the account xpub (it starts with xpub, ypub or zpub), and keep the private key on your device.
translation.That is an extended public key, but not: That is an extended public key, but not an account one. Coineda needs the key for a single account, as Ledger Live, Sparrow and Electrum export it - not the wallet master key.
translation.That does not look like an extended publ: That does not look like an extended public key. Copy the account xpub from your wallet - it is a long string starting with xpub, ypub or zpub, and it is case-sensitive.
translation.Your wallet account extended public key,: Your wallet account extended public key, not an address. Sparrow or Electrum connected to your device show it with its derivation path; Ledger Live has it under the account’s advanced logs. Ledger Live labels native-SegWit accounts "xpub" regardless, so Coineda works out the address type by checking the chain rather than trusting the prefix. One key covers one account, so a second Ledger Live account needs a second data source. It cannot spend - but treat it as private, since it reveals every address the wallet will ever use.
translation.One address per line, for addresses no x: One address per line, for addresses no xpub derives - a paper wallet, a cold address, an exchange deposit address. Only the addresses listed here are tracked, so one you own but never add stays invisible to Coineda.
translation.In Bitpanda, open your profile menu and: In Bitpanda, open your profile menu and go to API. Create a new key, tick only the read scopes listed below, and copy it before closing the dialog - Bitpanda shows a key once and never again. Coineda only ever reads: it cannot trade, withdraw or move anything. The key is stored on this device and travels only inside a checkpoint you create, which is encrypted.
translation.Bitpanda rejected this API key. Check th: Bitpanda rejected this API key. Check that it is correct and that it has not expired.
translation.Bitpanda refused the request before chec: Bitpanda refused the request before checking the key. This is its bot protection rather than anything wrong with your key - trying again later usually works.
translation.Could not reach Bitpanda. It may be unav: Could not reach Bitpanda. It may be unavailable right now.

translation.The Blockscout API to query. Leave this: The Blockscout API to query. Leave this empty to use the public eth.blockscout.com deployment, or point it at an instance you run yourself.
translation.The address to track, as 0x followed by: The address to track, as 0x followed by 40 hex characters. Only this address is tracked: ether in another address of yours stays invisible to Coineda until you add it as well. Reading an address reveals nothing private - it is public on the chain - and Coineda can only read.
translation.Add the Ethereum address to track, as 0x: Add the Ethereum address to track, as 0x followed by 40 hex characters.
translation.Could not reach this Blockscout instance: Could not reach this Blockscout instance. Check the URL, or try again later.
